subject: OpalView onramp: combined credit + commit collar request
messages:
From: Eleanor Park <eleanor@opalview.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-12 09:14 PST
Subject: Quick ask on trial/top-up while procurement finishes

Hi Ava,

Hope you’re well — we had a productive demo with Ben last week and the team is excited about Redwood for our query-answering microservice. Procurement wants to finish a security review before any contract, which will take ~3–4 weeks.

Two asks that would unblock a pilot this month:
- Can you extend the trial window by three weeks?
- Is there any way we can get a one-off credit top-up while procurement completes terms?

Budget is constrained; a short runway would let us validate latency at scale and get an exec sponsor comfortable. Curious what flexibility you can offer and whether we should loop in legal now.

Thanks,
Eleanor
Eleanor Park
Co-founder & COO, OpalView
Attachments: OpalView_Procurement_RFI.xlsx (xlsx)
From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor@opalview.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12 11:02 PST
Subject: Re: Quick ask on trial/top-up while procurement finishes

Eleanor — thanks for the note, happy to help.

Ben and I chatted about this; we can support a short runway but will need an internal approval for any credits beyond standard trial amounts. Two options we can propose to speed things along:

Option A (pilot-friendly, low friction)
- 3-week trial extension (no change to account status)
- $10k one-off usage credit applied to the trial project
- No commitment required; requires CS to monitor spend and a quick security attestation

Option B (commit + collar, better economics)
- 20% discount on year-one license if OpalView signs a 12-month minimum commitment within 45 days
- $25k credit applied against first three months of usage if commitment signed
- If OpalView does not commit within 45 days, credits convert to a 6-week extended trial and revert to standard pricing

If you think leadership will commit to a short-term purchase cadence, Option B gives more runway and aligns incentives. I’ll propose Option B to my manager for exec approval if OpalView is likely to lean that way.

If you’d like, I can circulate a one-page mutual action plan. I’ve included the procurement RFI you attached to make sure Legal/Compliance sees the right items.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-14 08:33 PST
Subject: Fwd: OpalView — approval ask (credit + collar)

Ava — flagged for exec review. Quick context: OpalView is a Series A fintech-ish analytics shop; likely $120k ARR in first 12 months if pilot converts (we model conservative usage). Competitive pressure from CloudX — they offered a 30% discount to try and expedite.

Requested concession (from Eleanor): 3-week extension + credit top-up. I recommend Option B (commit collar) because it protects our unit economics and materially increases chance of a closed-won.

Key asks for approval:
- Approve $25k credit to be applied against first three months if a 12-month commitment is signed within 45 days.
- Approve 20% first-year discount tied to the commitment.
- Approve a 45-day window for commitment; if not executed, credits revert to extended trial (6 weeks).

Risks: sets precedent for other small pilots; mitigation — credit is tied to a signed commitment and deal id. Also fine to require legal/finance pre-signed SOW template.

Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>; ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-15 10:12 PST
Subject: Re: Fwd: OpalView — approval ask (credit + collar)

Thanks for the summary. I’m supportive of Option B provided we add two guardrails:
1) Credits only draw down after invoice issuance against committed term (no upfront cash impact).
2) We include a cap: $25k max and clause that unused credits expire after 90 days from contract start.

Aditya — can you sign off on the 20% first-year discount + $25k credit collar? This is within our mid-market playbook but want exec OK because of the precedent and CloudX competitive push.

Marissa
VP, Sales Ops
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>; ava_chen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-18 17:03 PST
Subject: Re: Fwd: OpalView — approval ask (credit + collar)

All — I approve the deal path with the guardrails below. Please document in HubSpot and Legal:
- Approve 20% off year-one list for a 12-month committed agreement (minimum spend $60k annualized).
- Approve $25k credit collar to be applied only after the committed invoice is issued and paid; credits run against the first three billing cycles and expire 90 days after contract start if unused.
- Timebox: OpalView must sign within 45 days of offer; if not, credit reverts to a 6-week extended trial and discount is void.
- Require OPV to complete our standard security checklist (already requested) prior to production load.

Ava/Ben — please send Eleanor the MA plan and draft term sheet reflecting these exact guardrails. Good work moving quickly.

-Aditya
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
